trainers.strategy: Rock Tomb creates a visible speed tax; Onix gets one guaranteed action.

challenge.strategy: Sandstone Bastion: Hippopotas raises eight turns of sand, so every Rock member's Special Defense rises by half and the special Water Gun / Mega Drain plan of Normal stops one-shotting. Storm Drain Lileep eats Water, Flame Body Carkol burns contact Grass and Fighting and hits Grass with Fire, and Sturdy plus Weakness Policy turns one big super-effective hit on Onix into a +2 sweep. The answer is physical, multi-hit and status pressure, not one type.
challenge.ace_math_change: Sturdy guarantees Onix survives the first hit and Weakness Policy rewards a single super-effective blow; multi-hit moves (Arm Thrust, Fury Cutter), chip and paralysis break it cleanly.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: Hippopotas's sand is announced on turn one and Lileep's Storm Drain on the first Water move; Route 1's Machop, Pawmi, Marill, Krabby (Metal Claw) and Mareep (Thunder Wave) are the physical, multi-hit and status tools, and Normal's lesson (two types) still helps.

trainers.strategy: Horsea starts rain, Lombre uses it, and Starmie controls speed when the weather ends.
trainers.ace_math_change: Icy Wind changes turn order; Recover asks the player to maintain pressure.

normal.strategy: Horsea starts rain, Lombre uses it, and Starmie controls speed when the weather ends.

challenge.strategy: Undertow: no rain and no speed race. A slow attrition team where each obvious answer is absorbed or punished: Yawn forces switches, Toxic Spikes poisons every switch-in, Liquid Ooze Tentacool hurts the Mega Drain users, Lightning Rod Goldeen eats Electric and Drill Runs the Electric types, Skill Link Shellder shreds Grass, and Huge Power Azumarill revenges with Aqua Jet. Scald burns the physical answers.
challenge.ace_math_change: Starmie trades Normal's Icy Wind speed control for Scald burns, Thunder Wave and Recover: the player wins by pressure from two sides, not by outspeeding it.
challenge.line_obviousness: clear after scouting: Goldeen's Lightning Rod and Tentacool's Liquid Ooze show on the first hit; the plan is split Electric, non-draining Grass (Razor Leaf), Dark for the two Psychic types (Nuzleaf) and Ground for Tentacool.

trainers.strategy: Paralysis sets the pace; mixed Electric attackers punish a team built around only one wall.
trainers.ace_math_change: Raichu may set up, but Ground remains a clean answer from the first hit.

availability_contract.note: The route teaches a Ground immunity plan and a separate resistance or priority plan.

normal.strategy: Paralysis sets the pace; mixed Electric attackers punish a team built around only one wall.

challenge.strategy: Live Wire: three of six cannot be touched by Ground (Kilowattrel's Flying, Emolga's Flying, Vikavolt's Levitate), and the three grounded ones punish a Ground switch-in with Scald, Energy Ball, Grass Knot, Surf and Ice Punch. Volt Switch pivots the floaters in front of the Ground answer. The answer is Rock for the fliers, Ground only for the grounded, and Volt Absorb or bulk for the rest.
challenge.ace_math_change: Pawmot replaces Normal's Raichu as the closer: Mach Punch priority and Ice Punch mean a lone Ground answer loses the last exchange; Thick Fat Hariyama and the Rock line win it.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: the lead is a Ground-immune flier, which says 'not Ground' on turn one; Mt Clay's Rhyhorn, Rockruff and Makuhita and the badge-1 Rock Slide TM are the tools, and Quagsire's Water Absorb walls Lanturn.

trainers.strategy: Sun is the only engine: Bellossom starts it, two attackers exploit it, and Vileplume closes.
trainers.ace_math_change: Coba Berry buys one turn against Flying while leaving Ice and Fire completely intact.

normal.strategy: Sun is the only engine: Bellossom starts it, two attackers exploit it, and Vileplume closes.
normal.ace_math_change: Coba Berry buys one turn against Flying while leaving Ice and Fire completely intact.

challenge.strategy: Rain Garden: the opposite weather to Normal's sun. Prankster Whimsicott sets eight turns of rain and Tailwind before anything moves, rain halves the Fire answer Normal teaches, and Swift Swim Ludicolo hits Fire with Hydro Pump and Flying with Ice Beam. Ferroseed's Gyro Ball and Breloom's Mach Punch punish Ice, Cradily's Rock Slide punishes Flying and Fire, Contrary Lurantis gets stronger from its own Superpower.
challenge.ace_math_change: Ludicolo, not Vileplume, closes: Grass/Water takes Fire neutral (halved again in rain) and Ice neutral, so the answer is Poison, Flying that survives Ice Beam, or a Dark type that ignores Prankster.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: rain falls on turn one and says 'Fire is weaker here'; the Dark types (Houndour, Stunky) north-east of Route 4 ignore Prankster, and Poison (Tentacruel, Skuntank) hits Whimsicott four times over and Ludicolo twice.

trainers.strategy: Direct poison starts a clock; Venoshock converts that clock into pressure while Drapion checks Psychic.
trainers.ace_math_change: Tinted Lens prevents passive resistance from being the whole answer; speed control and priority still work.

normal.strategy: Direct poison starts a clock; Venoshock converts that clock into pressure while Drapion checks Psychic.
normal.ace_math_change: Tinted Lens prevents passive resistance from being the whole answer; speed control and priority still work.

challenge.strategy: Ambush: Ariados lays Toxic Spikes behind a Focus Sash, so every switch costs poison, and the rest punish Normal's Ground and Psychic answers with coverage: Skuntank is immune to Psychic and Sucker Punches it, Roserade's Giga Drain and Tentacruel's Scald hit the Ground types, Dry Skin Toxicroak drinks the Water answer. Glimmora closes, and Toxic Debris lays more Toxic Spikes whenever it is struck physically.
challenge.ace_math_change: Glimmora replaces Venomoth: a Focus Sash ace that takes Ground four times over but answers the slow Ground switch-in with Energy Ball. Speed, a Steel type (immune to the poison) or special Water wins.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: Toxic Spikes on turn one says 'bring Steel or keep switches few'; Bronzong (Mt Vessu) and Excadrill (Route 5) shrug off the poison, Xatu and Medicham take the Psychic line, and Empoleon's Water beats Glimmora.

trainers.strategy: Two setters create a slow phase; Alakazam closes after Trick Room expires.
trainers.ace_math_change: Magic Guard Life Orb makes the fast closer dangerous without covering its Dark weakness.

normal.strategy: Two setters create a slow phase; Alakazam closes after Trick Room expires.

challenge.strategy: Mind Field: no Trick Room. Indeedee's Psychic Surge lays eight turns of Psychic Terrain, which powers Expanding Force and stops every priority move against Sabrina's grounded team, so Normal's Sucker Punch answer fails. Gallade's Close Combat and Gardevoir's Moonblast punish the Dark answer; Reuniclus's Focus Blast and Espeon's Magic Bounce (Taunt, Toxic and Thunder Wave reflected) punish the rest.
challenge.ace_math_change: Alakazam keeps Magic Guard but carries Focus Sash, Nasty Plot, Focus Blast and Dazzling Gleam: Dark types are no longer safe against it, and priority cannot touch it while the terrain lasts.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: the terrain announces itself on Indeedee's entry; Ghost (Banette) and Poison (Scolipede, Skuntank) handle the Fairy and Fighting halves that wall Dark, and the Dark attackers win once the eight turns run out.

trainers.strategy: Sun changes Water math; Arcanine is the one Water check and Charizard creates a visible damage race.
trainers.ace_math_change: Solar Power changes neutral thresholds, but Rock and Ground remain clean answers.

normal.strategy: Sun changes Water math; Arcanine is the one Water check and Charizard creates a visible damage race.
normal.ace_math_change: Solar Power changes neutral thresholds, but Rock and Ground remain clean answers.

challenge.strategy: Wildfire: no sun, so Normal's lesson about weather does not apply. Gale Wings Talonflame sets Tailwind and burns the physical answer, then the team punishes Water directly: Chandelure's Energy Ball, Scovillain (Grass/Fire, neutral to Water and Ground) and Infernape's Grass Knot. Charizard Dragon Dances, and Volcarona Quiver Dances behind Giga Drain. Water alone is not enough; Rock (Stealth Rock, Rock Slide, Stone Edge) is the type the team cannot cover.
challenge.ace_math_change: Volcarona replaces Charizard as the closer: Quiver Dance plus Giga Drain beats Water and Ground, but Rock hits it four times over and Stealth Rock takes half its health.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: Tailwind and a burn on turn one say 'not a slow Water team'; the Rock line (Rhyhorn to Rhydon, Lycanroc, Coalossal with Stealth Rock) and Gyarados (Grass is only neutral on it) are on Routes 3, 4 and 7.

trainers.strategy: Sand changes thresholds; Persian breaks tempo and Rhyperior advertises its setup turn.
trainers.ace_math_change: Solid Rock rewards setting up Rhyperior in view of the player while Water and Grass remain valid.

availability_contract.note: Two independent plans are available: split Water/Grass offense, or Ground immunity plus Fighting and priority.

normal.strategy: Sand changes thresholds; Persian breaks tempo and Rhyperior advertises its setup turn.
normal.ace_math_change: Solid Rock rewards setting up Rhyperior in view of the player while Water and Grass remain valid.

challenge.strategy: Grand Strategy: no sand. Every member is chosen against Normal's Water/Grass answer. Claydol (Levitate) sets Stealth Rock and Ice Beams Grass; Storm Drain Gastrodon absorbs Water; Gliscor (Poison Heal) takes Grass neutrally and resists Fighting; Donphan's Ice Shard and Gunk Shot hit Grass and Fairy; Mold Breaker Excadrill's Earthquake goes through Levitate. Garchomp closes: neutral to both Water and Grass.
challenge.ace_math_change: Garchomp replaces Rhyperior: Water and Grass are only neutral, Focus Sash guarantees a Swords Dance, and the clean answer becomes Ice (four times over), Fairy or Dragon, with the player's own Stealth Rock breaking the sash.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: Claydol's Stealth Rock and Gastrodon's Storm Drain show early that Water is not the plan; Ice (Snover, Bergmite from Route 4), Fairy (Tinkatink on Long Isle and the southern plateau, Ralts from Pallet) and Gyarados's Intimidate carry it.

trainers.strategy: Snow, hazards and speed denial make resource preservation matter across the whole fight.
trainers.ace_math_change: Assault Vest turns Lapras into a special sponge while Freeze-Dry reverses the usual Water counter.

normal.strategy: Snow, hazards and speed denial make resource preservation matter across the whole fight.

challenge.strategy: Snow Fortress: Snow Warning Abomasnow sets snow (Ice types' Defense up by half) and an eight-turn Aurora Veil, which halves the damage of every hit. Behind it come physical setup threats that punish Normal's Fire/Fighting/Rock/Steel answers: Shell Smash Cloyster with Rock Blast for Fire, Crabominable's Drain Punch and Earthquake for Steel and Rock, Ice Scales Frosmoth halving special Fire, and a Slush Rush Belly Drum Cetitan.
challenge.ace_math_change: Lapras keeps its Freeze-Dry but trades Assault Vest for Weakness Policy and Heal Bell: under Veil one super-effective hit does not KO it and powers it up, and Heal Bell undoes the burns and paralysis a status plan relies on.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: snow and the Veil go up on turn one; the answers are a Taunt or a fast KO on Abomasnow, a screen-breaker (Brick Break) or Infiltrator Chandelure, Thick Fat Hariyama, and priority for Cetitan.

trainers.strategy: Fake Out, removal, priority and mixed physical pressure punish a team that reaches the League without tempo tools.
trainers.ace_math_change: White Herb restores the defense drops from Close Combat and consumes itself to activate Unburden.

normal.strategy: Fake Out, removal, priority and mixed physical pressure punish a team that reaches the League without tempo tools.

challenge.strategy: Iron Discipline: every member covers the types that beat Fighting. Scrafty is immune to Psychic and Ice Punches Flying; Hitmonchan's elemental punches hit Flying and Water; Pure Power Medicham's Bullet Punch and Poison Jab hit Fairy; Quaquaval speeds up with every Aqua Step; Conkeldurr's Stone Edge and Knock Off hit Flying and Psychic. Annihilape's Defiant turns Intimidate into +2 Attack.
challenge.ace_math_change: Annihilape replaces Hitmonlee: a Ghost/Fighting ace immune to Normal and Fighting moves and to Fake Out, whose Rage Fist grows each time it is hit. Ghost, Psychic, Flying or Fairy that hits it once and hard wins, and Intimidate backfires.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: Scrafty's Intimidate and Fake Out lead read like Normal's, but the first Psychic switch-in meets a Dark type; Tinkaton (Steel/Fairy) resists Bullet Punch and is immune to Poison Jab, and Banette is immune to every Fighting move.

trainers.strategy: Burns, Taunt, Trick and priority deny clean setup and force the player to manage status across six different Ghost patterns.
trainers.ace_math_change: Focus Sash guarantees Gengar a response and makes priority or prior hazard control part of the answer.

normal.strategy: Burns, Taunt, Trick and priority deny clean setup and force the player to manage status across six different Ghost patterns.

challenge.strategy: The Slow Haunting: Trick Room Ghosts. Cofagrigus sets Trick Room behind a Mental Herb, so the first Taunt does not stop it, and Trevenant can set it again. Under it the slow hitters move first: No Guard Golurk's Dynamic Punch always lands on the Dark answer, Mimikyu's Disguise and Play Rough punish Dark too, Prankster Sableye burns and Encores, and Cursed Body Jellicent walls special attackers.
challenge.ace_math_change: Golurk replaces Gengar: slow on purpose, an Assault Vest for special Dark Pulses, and Dynamic Punch that never misses. The answer is to run out or reverse the five turns (Protect, a pivot, a Trick Room of the player's own) and then hit its Water, Grass, Ice, Ghost or Dark weakness.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: Trick Room on turn one says 'your fast Dark sweeper moves last'; slow answers (Kingambit, Rhydon, Bronzong) thrive under it, Steel (Kingambit, Tinkaton) beats Mimikyu, and Sableye's Prankster fails against a Dark type.

trainers.strategy: Aerodactyl sets the pace, each midgame member attacks a different Dragon answer, and Dragonite is the only dedicated setup closer.
trainers.ace_math_change: Multiscale plus Weakness Policy punishes an undisciplined super-effective first hit and changes priority damage thresholds.

normal.strategy: Aerodactyl sets the pace, each midgame member attacks a different Dragon answer, and Dragonite is the only dedicated setup closer.

challenge.strategy: Dragon's Armour: Dragons that Ice and Fairy do not simply delete. Duraludon (Steel/Dragon) takes both neutrally, sets Stealth Rock and paralyses; Tyrantrum (Rock/Dragon) Dragon Dances and Head Smashes Ice; Sniper Kingdra and Hydreigon carry Flash Cannon for Fairy; Assault Vest Goodra answers Fairy with Sludge Bomb and Steel with Fire Blast, and Gooey slows the physical Ice Shard user. Fighting and Ground hit four of the six.
challenge.ace_math_change: Dragonite keeps Multiscale but swaps Weakness Policy and Extreme Speed for Heavy-Duty Boots and Roost: the player's Stealth Rock no longer breaks Multiscale, and Roost restores it. Phazing, Haze, Encore, Taunt or two Ice hits in a row win.
challenge.line_obviousness: moderate: a Steel/Dragon lead that takes Ice and Fairy only neutrally says 'not Ice alone'; Excadrill and Victory Road's Machamp take Duraludon and Tyrantrum, Fairy and Ice still take the back four, and the ace needs a plan for its boosts.

trainers.strategy: Blue recombines the campaign's lessons: tempo lead, sleep, hazards, Intimidate, speed, and a setup ace with no single type shortcut.
trainers.ace_math_change: White Herb erases Shell Smash's defensive cost, forcing the player to stop the setup or answer a full-speed mixed-coverage closer.

normal.strategy: Blue recombines the campaign's lessons: tempo lead, sleep, hazards, Intimidate, speed, and a setup ace with no single type shortcut.
normal.ace_math_change: White Herb erases Shell Smash's defensive cost, forcing the player to stop the setup or answer a full-speed mixed-coverage closer.

challenge.strategy: The Champion's counter-team: no member of Normal's six. Aerodactyl leads with Stealth Rock and Taunt; No Guard Machamp's Dynamic Punch always confuses; Technician Scizor pivots and Bullet Punches Fairy and Ice; Air Balloon Magnezone floats over Ground until the first hit; Choice Specs Gengar is immune to the Fighting that kills Tyranitar. Normal's lesson (speed control, hazard control, a balanced six) still applies; the answers change.
challenge.ace_math_change: Tyranitar replaces Blastoise: a Dragon Dance ace whose Sand Stream raises its Special Defense by half. Fighting (four times over) wins only once Gengar is gone; Water, Grass, Ground, Steel, Bug and Fairy each hit it twice over.
challenge.line_obviousness: low: nothing on the field repeats Normal's Blue, so the player scouts as they go; the balanced six Normal teaches still wins, but which member answers which slot changes (Fire for Scizor, Ground after the Balloon pops, Dark for Gengar, Fighting or Water for Tyranitar).

trainers.lesson: Priority after a speed tax.

dialogue_text.pre: This cave slows you down before it beats you up. Hope you kept something quick.
dialogue_text.player_win: You had something fast left over. Fine.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Too slow. Go back up and get faster.

dialogue_text.player_win: You ended it before the poison could add up.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Every turn you sat there poisoned was mine.

dialogue_text.player_win: You found an answer that did not care about the sun.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Too hot for you. Go and cool off.

dialogue_text.pre: One burn and your big hitters are done. Then Mudsdale. Got anything that isn't muscle?
dialogue_text.player_win: Good. You switched tools when the map changed.
dialogue_text.player_loss: All muscle, and I burned it.

dialogue_text.pre: Break's over. Once the sand's up, my side takes hits yours can't.
dialogue_text.player_win: You did not trust yesterday's damage numbers.
dialogue_text.player_loss: The sand was chipping you from the first turn.

trainers.lesson: Trick Room reversal.

dialogue_text.pre: For the next few turns, slow goes first. Live through the room, then move.
dialogue_text.player_win: You knew when not to race.
dialogue_text.player_loss: All that speed, and my room made it worthless.

dialogue_text.pre: In the rain both of mine do their jobs faster. Try and split them up.
dialogue_text.player_win: You got between the rain and the coverage. Nice.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Still raining. Go and dry off.

trainers.lesson: Switch cost and immunity.

dialogue_text.pre: Switch carelessly in this cut and the rocks bill you. Pick who stays in.
dialogue_text.player_win: Not one switch you didn't need. Good.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Every switch cost you. Should have counted.

trainers.lesson: Setup denial and setup race.

dialogue_text.pre: I stop your plan, then I run mine. Got a backup?
dialogue_text.player_win: You had that ready before I'd even started. Annoying.
dialogue_text.player_loss: First plan stopped, no second one. Done.

mode_intent.normal: Ten short cave examinations revisit one learned tool each across a 4 / rest / 6 ascent.
mode_intent.challenge: The same ten cave stands, levels and caps, each previewing an engine of the Challenge League: Lorelei's Aurora Veil and snow, Agatha's Ghosts and Trick Room, Bruno's No Guard and Intimidate, Blue's sand, Lance's rain and Steel-dragons. One held item per fight, and a five-member final examiner.

trainers.lesson: Tailwind final examination.

dialogue_text.pre: My Crobat carries a Focus Sash. It will get the wind up. The exam is what you do after that.
dialogue_text.player_win: You did not need the first turn. You needed the right six.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Fail. Come back with a better six.

trainers.lesson: Sturdy holds one more turn: a single strong hit is not a plan.

dialogue_text.pre: Every stone in this hall was squared by hand. Let's see how square you are.
dialogue_text.player_win: Cut clean. The foreman will want to see that.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Rough edges. Go back down and dress them.

trainers.lesson: Rock Tomb slows the answer you were counting on.

dialogue_text.pre: You came over the wall. Most people take the stack that goes nowhere.
dialogue_text.player_win: Good climbing, better battling. Brock is through the lit slot.
dialogue_text.player_loss: The wall's still there. Climb it again when you're ready.

trainers.lesson: Rapid Spin and Rock Polish buy speed: hit before the stone gets going.

dialogue_text.pre: Last cart before the boss. Everything you brought up here, I haul back down.
dialogue_text.player_win: Fair load. Brock's just up the ladder. Mind the soot.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Too heavy for you yet. Back down the beams with you.

trainers.lesson: Swift Swim and priority: the water moves first unless you make it wait.

dialogue_text.pre: Nobody walks up to Misty's door. Whatever brought you, the water decides the rest.
dialogue_text.player_win: You keep your head above it. Go on in.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Swim back to the shallows and catch your breath.

trainers.lesson: Recover undoes chip damage: hit hard or not at all.

dialogue_text.pre: Last check before the pool. Misty doesn't wait for anyone who can't keep up.
dialogue_text.player_win: Strong strokes. She's at the far rim.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Out of the water. Rest, then try again.

trainers.lesson: Thunder Wave first, damage second: paralysis is the real attack.

dialogue_text.pre: Mind the tower, it's live. So am I.
dialogue_text.player_win: Clean break in the circuit. Up you go.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Tripped the breaker. Reset and come back.

trainers.lesson: Charge Beam builds: end it before the third turn.

dialogue_text.pre: Three runs and only one of them is carrying. Did you read which?
dialogue_text.player_win: You can read a board. The Lieutenant's past the duct.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Grounded. Walk the catwalk again and think.

trainers.lesson: Electro Ball hits harder the faster it is: slow it down or outpace it.

dialogue_text.pre: You walked the whole catwalk to get here. The cable run is mine.
dialogue_text.player_win: Line's yours. Keep your hands off the rails on the way over.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Tripped the breaker. Reset and come back along the catwalk.

trainers.lesson: Powders are the threat; the damage is just weather.

dialogue_text.pre: Mind the beds. Mind me, too.
dialogue_text.player_win: You walk the canopy like you planted it.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Wilted. Take some sun and come back up.

trainers.lesson: Regenerator and Leech Seed: a slow fight favours the garden.

dialogue_text.pre: One line of piers still has its second stone. You saw which?
dialogue_text.player_win: Erika is in the court below. Drop carefully.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Down in the mulch again. The ladder is by the wall.

trainers.lesson: Stun Spore is the plan, not the damage: keep a cure or a switch ready.

dialogue_text.pre: Nobody gets up the living bough without a scratch. Let's give you one.
dialogue_text.player_win: Steady footing. The high canopy is all yours.
dialogue_text.player_loss: The bough threw you. Breathe, and climb it again.

trainers.lesson: Sucker Punch punishes the slow, careful setup.

dialogue_text.pre: You came in loud. Koga will have heard you already.
dialogue_text.player_win: Quieter than you look. Take the reed stair.
dialogue_text.player_loss: The fen keeps what it catches. Dry off and try again.

trainers.lesson: Toxic is a clock: every switch spends your time.

dialogue_text.pre: The tank is breathing. Do you know where it comes up?
dialogue_text.player_win: You read the water. The flue's below.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Too long under. Breathe, then come back.

trainers.lesson: Toxic Spikes and a pivot: the damage comes on entry.

dialogue_text.pre: Up the flue and still standing. Koga will be pleased, if you get past me.
dialogue_text.player_win: Go on. He has been watching you since the door.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Back down the chute. The fen is patient.

trainers.lesson: Calm Mind turns a slow special attacker into a wall: break it early.

dialogue_text.pre: Three of the stacks stop short. One doesn't. You knew that before you came in.
dialogue_text.player_win: You read well. The gallery is above.
dialogue_text.player_loss: You trusted the wrong stack. Read again.

trainers.lesson: Hypnosis misses often; a team that plans for sleep never needs luck.

dialogue_text.pre: The eye in the arch is looking at you, not me.
dialogue_text.player_win: You see clearly. The turret ladder is north.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Your eyes lied to you. Rest them.

trainers.lesson: Trick Room-style speed control: the slow side moves first here.

dialogue_text.pre: One more lens before hers. Look through me first.
dialogue_text.player_win: Sabrina is waiting at the top. She knew you would come.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Fogged. Come back when you can see.

trainers.lesson: Calm Mind stacks every turn it is left alone: pressure it early.

dialogue_text.pre: The gallery's west walk is shelved by thought. You'll need yours.
dialogue_text.player_win: Your mind held. The north arm is ahead.
dialogue_text.player_loss: You lost the thread. Go back to the stacks and find it.

trainers.lesson: Flame Charge snowballs: stop the first speed boost.

dialogue_text.pre: The spoil steps are hot. So's my team.
dialogue_text.player_win: You'll do. Mind the broken flight, it goes nowhere.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Cool off by the furnace and try again.

trainers.lesson: Nasty Plot plus a fast Fire type: pressure it before it sets up.

dialogue_text.pre: The gantry is the only way up. I'm the only way past it.
dialogue_text.player_win: Readings are good. Up to the gallery.
dialogue_text.player_loss: The vent was hotter than you. Down you go.

trainers.lesson: Sun boosts every Fire move: change the weather or lose the race.

dialogue_text.pre: Four hoods, one breathing. You have to get past me to pick.
dialogue_text.player_win: The leap is yours. Blaine is below the flue.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Wrong hood. The geyser will bring you back up.

trainers.lesson: Flame Charge speeds it up with every hit: answer the first one.

dialogue_text.pre: Halfway up the gantry is where the heat starts. Keep climbing if you can.
dialogue_text.player_win: You took the heat. The gallery's at the top.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Burned out on the stair. Cool off and come back up.

trainers.lesson: Sand Stream chip and Sand Rush: the field fights for them.

dialogue_text.pre: You found the sap. Most stand in the yard waiting for a door.
dialogue_text.player_win: Down the heading, then. Mind the shoring.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Cave-in. Climb out and come back down.

trainers.lesson: Dig dodges a turn: use it to switch, not to wait.

dialogue_text.pre: The heading's shored for one. You'll fight me in it.
dialogue_text.player_win: Through, then. The tower stair is round the corner.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Back to the sap. The drill starts over.

trainers.lesson: Rock Slide flinches and Lightning Rod: plan around both.

dialogue_text.pre: Nobody comes up the stair without coming past me.
dialogue_text.player_win: Up the stair. The walk is open.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Back to the drift. Try the stair again when you can.

trainers.lesson: Sheer Force and Earth Power: the last guard hits like the boss.

dialogue_text.pre: The gate walk is mine. The Boss sees everything from here.
dialogue_text.player_win: You held the line. He's at the end of the walk.
dialogue_text.player_loss: Back to the yard. The drill starts over.
